newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Harriet field to supply gas to mine.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Harriet field to supply gas to mine.

text.p: Apache Energy Ltd said on Thursday its part-owned Harriet Joint Venture offshore gas field will supply natural gas to the Wiluna gold mine in Western Australia when a new gas-fired power station replaces diesel generators at the mine.
The power station's natural gas requirements are expected to exceed two terajoules a day, with the first gas sales scheduled for October 1997, Apache said.
The agreement was reached between Apache and the operator of the mine, Wiluna Mines Ltd and runs for 10 years, Apache said.
The gas will be produced from the existing Harriet Joint Venture offshore gas gathering facilities and processing plant on Varanus Island, Apache said.
It will be delivered over a distance of some 960 km via the sales gas pipeline from Varanus Island to shore and then via the Goldfields Gas Transmission (GGT) pipeline.
A new eight km pipeline lateral will be built from the GGT pipeline to the mine.

This agreement between Wiluna and the Harriet venture is the first gas sales agreement to be made for supplies through the GGT pipeline outside of those signed with the companies associated with the ownership of the GGT pipeline, Apache said.

Partners in the Harriet Joint Venture are Apache (22.5 percent), Mobil Corp (25 percent), Kuwait Foreign Petroleum Exploration Corp (19.3 percent), Novus Petroleum Ltd (12.5 percent), Hardy Oil and Gas Plc (8.4 percent), Tap Oil NL (12.2 percent) and New World Oil and Developments Pty Ltd (0.1 percent).
